extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and quality/formatting standards for filing, processing, assigning, amending, and reporting on ex parte reexamination proceedings at the USPTO, including PALM/PAIR handling and examiner assignment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Request for Ex Parte Reexamination in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of filing of all complete ex parte reexamination requests will be published in the Official Gazette, approximately 4-5 weeks after filing. Both reexamination requests assigned a filing date and Director-initiated orders to reexamine made without a request will be announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination preprocessing staff of the CRU completes a form with information needed for printing. The Official Gazette notice appears under 'Requests for Ex Parte Reexamination Filed' and will include the name of any requestor along with the other items set forth in 37 CFR 1.11(c). A record of requests filed will also be located in the Patent Search Room and CRU preprocessing area; office personnel may use PALM to determine if a request has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive Notice to Patent Owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If all efforts to correspond with the patent owner fail because no current address is available, publication in the Official Gazette of (A) the notice of the filing of a request for reexamination, or (B) the notice of the ordering of reexamination at the initiative of the Director, will serve as constructive notice to the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when actual notice cannot be delivered; publication serves as constructive notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of Request Corrections (preprocessing area handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: All processing of submissions to cure an incomplete request for ex parte reexamination is carried out in the preprocessing area of the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions should be marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' as discussed in MPEP §2224 so they may be promptly forwarded to the reexamination preprocessing staff of the CRU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access to Reexamination Files
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public via Public PAIR on the USPTO website; members of the public can view the entire content of the reexamination file with the exception of non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps to access Public PAIR are provided (site index → Electronic Business Center → Status & View Documents → Patent Application Information Retrieval → select 'Control Number' and enter control number → Search). Copies may be ordered from Document Services Division (provide control number), requested by e-mail to dsd@uspto.gov, cost may be charged to credit card/deposit account, or obtained from IFW via PAIR. Certified copies available via CD-ROM from OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining if a Reexamination Request Was Filed (PAIR/PALM procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Public PAIR (Internet) or PALM (USPTO Intranet) to determine whether a reexamination request has been filed for a given patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet steps: go to uspto.gov → Site Index → E → Electronic Business Center → Status & View Documents → select 'Patent Application Information Retrieval' and 'Patent Number' → enter patent number → Search → Continuity Data → scroll to 'Child Continuity Data' to find reexamination (90/… for ex parte, 95/… for inter partes). Intranet PALM steps: ptoweb → PALM → General Information → enter patent # → Search → Continuity Data. Note ~10 day lag between filing and PALM data entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees Applicable to Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: There are fees for the reexamination request, for addition of claims (excess claims fees), for extensions of time, and for appeals/briefs/oral hearing; no fee is required for issue of the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) (request), 1.20(c)(3) & (c)(4) (excess claims), 1.550(c) (extension), 41.20(b) (appeal/brief/hearing). Petitions relating to reexamination (37 CFR 1.137/1.182/1.183) require fees (37 CFR 1.17 subparagraphs). Small entity reductions available for certain fees (37 CFR 1.137 petition fee, excess claim fees, appeal/brief/oral hearing fees) but NOT available for the reexamination filing fee, extension of time fees, nor petitions under 1.182 and 1.183. In merged proceedings only a single fee is needed even if multiple copies required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Mailing/Transmittal Form for Requester Address
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal form with the requester's address is used to forward copies of Office actions (and any references cited) to the requester to avoid retyping the address for each mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the patent owner is the requester, no such form is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of Making Amendments in Reexamination (§1.530 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with §1.530; an amendment paper directs specified changes to the patent specification (including claims) or drawings and may accompany owner-request or be submitted during prosecution where permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment papers may be submitted with a request by patent owner under §1.510(e), as part of a patent owner statement under §1.530(b), or during prosecution per §1.550(a) or §1.937 where permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification Amendments Must Present Entire Added/Rewritten Paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification other than to the claims must be made by submission of the entire text of any added or rewritten paragraph including markings pursuant to paragraph (f) of §1.530, except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise point in the specification must be identified where any added or rewritten paragraph is located. This applies whether amendments are on paper or compact disc per §§1.96 and 1.825.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Amendments Must Include Entire Text and Markings
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim being proposed to be changed and of each new claim proposed to be added. For any changed claim, a parenthetical 'amended', 'twice amended', etc., should follow the claim number; each changed or added claim must include markings pursuant to paragraph (f), except a canceled claim may be canceled by statement without presenting the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims proposed to be changed or added must be presented in full; cancellations may be by statement canceling the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings Amendments Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval. Upon approval, only new sheets including changes and complying with §1.84 must be filed. Amended figures identified as 'Amended', added figures as 'New', canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketches show proposed changes in red; after examiner approval submit new sheets per §1.84; canceled figures use brackets rather than strike-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of Claims and Support for Claim Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims pursuant to §1.530(d), pages separate from the pages containing the changes must supply the status (pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment of all patent claims and all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status and support must be on separate pages distinct from the amended text pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes Shown by Markings (brackets and underlining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must show matter to be omitted enclosed in brackets and matter to be added underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings pursuant to paragraph (f) of §1.530 govern presentation of additions and deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of Patent Claims Preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered; numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on renumbering; added claims follow existing highest claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments Must Not Enlarge Claim Scope or Introduce New Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. No amendment, other than cancellation of claims, will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on enlarging claim scope or adding new matter; timing restrictions relative to patent expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments Not Legally Effective Until Reexamination Certificate Issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are entered for examination purposes but have no legal effect until issuance and publication of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation Requirements — Full Copy of Amended Text
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments in reexamination proceedings, including examiner's amendments, must be presented in the form of a full copy of the text of each claim which is amended and each paragraph of the description which is amended (i.e., the entire claim or paragraph must be presented for any amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate ALL of the changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text of the patent under reexamination. See MPEP §2250 for format examples and §2270 for clerical handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW Entry and Clerical Handling of Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: For an IFW reexamination file, the amendment paper is designated by consecutive letters (A, B, C...), each entry blocked by two lines and given successive numbers (A1, A2...), marked-up copies scanned into IFW file history, canceled claims/paragraphs surrounded by brackets (not lined through), and the marked-up amendment document scanned into IFW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure details: copy of claims filed with request printed from IFW file history; a line drawn through any claim(s) or paragraphs amended with substituted copy indicated by amendment letter/number; canceled patent claims are bracketed, not lined through; amendment documents scanned into IFW; claim numbering must not be changed. See MPEP §2270 for clerical handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM Record Systems and Event Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The PALM system is used to support reexamination: obtain data on reexamination files, monitor movement of paper files, and monitor/report major processing events. Events are permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' of PALM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination e-file may be viewed on IFW. Data in PALM includes patent owner, requester, contents, status, and related proceedings. Events to be reported include: determination mailed (denial), determination mailed (grant), petition for reconsideration received, decision on petition mailed (denied/granted), owner response to determination received, requester reply received, mailing of all examiner actions, receipt of owner's responses and Office receipt dates, and additional events reported by Reexamination Preprocessing Unit. Status representatives of these events also displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM Status/Weekly Tickler Reports — Timeliness Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Various weekly 'tickler' reports generated from PALM indicate when deadlines are approaching and highlight requests needing action to ensure reexaminations are processed with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified reports include: Requests Not Yet Received in CRU (indicator of workload/stragglers); Requests Not Yet Assigned to an Examiner (highlight those not assigned by 6th week — should be docketed immediately); Requests Which Should Be Taken Up for Determination (assigned but no determination mailed and 6th week past — should be taken up for determination); Requests For Which Determinations Should Be Prepared (assigned but no determination mailed and 2nd month past — determinations should be in final stages); Requests For Which Determinations Should Have Been Mailed (assigned with no determination mailed and 10th week past — should be mailed immediately); Overdue Determinations (no determination mailed and 3rd month past — should always be zero); Overdue Petitions for Reconsideration of a Denial (6 weeks after determination mailed); Overdue Owner Responses to Determinations (10 weeks after determination mailed when owner has not filed response); Overdue Requester Responses to Statements (10 weeks after owner response); Overdue First Ex Parte Actions (6 weeks after request available for ex parte prosecution); Overdue Action or Examiner's Answer (2 months for second/subsequent action); Overdue Advisory Action (1 month after filing of owner response to previous final action); Overdue Owner Response (4 months since action rendered); Overdue Certificates (3 months after NIRC mailed with no issue date assigned); Requests With Prolonged Prosecution (15 months since filing without certificate). Asterisked items require immediate action and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of Reexamination — Art Unit and Examiner Selection Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests should normally be assigned to the CRU art unit which examines the technology in which the patent is classified, and to a primary examiner other than the examiner who originally examined the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU SPE will assign to an examiner most familiar with the claimed subject matter but different from the original examiner(s) who examined the patent application (including conferees). Exceptions include rare situations where the original examiner is the only one with adequate knowledge — such an assignment must be approved by the CRU Director and that approval must be stated in the decision on the request. If an earlier concluded reexamination examiner generally excluded, but if the earlier reexamination is still ongoing the same examiner will be assigned the new reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Copending Reissue and Reexamination Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Special assignment rules when reissue and reexamination are copending: generally assign reexamination to an examiner who did not examine the original patent even if that examiner handles the reissue; if proceedings merge OPLA assigns merged proceedings appropriately, but if the examiner was involved in original examination a different TC examiner will be assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination ordered and reissue later merged, merged proceeding handled by TC examiner handling reissue unless involvement in original exam precludes assignment; if reexamination pending and reissue filed, QAS will ensure reissue is not assigned until reexamination decision made. Process for notifying OPLA and hand-delivering paper files if needed. If reexamination not yet ordered and reissue filed, QAS awaits owner statements and replies or time expiration then notifies OPLA for merger consideration per MPEP §§2249–2251 and §§2283/2285.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and Procedure for Inadvertent Assignment to Original Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is inadvertently assigned to an 'original examiner', the patent owner or third-party requester who objects must promptly file a paper alerting the Office; any request challenging assignment must be made within two months of the first Office action or communication indicating the examiner assignment, or reassignment will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassignment will be addressed case-by-case; assignment to original examiner alone is not grounds to vacate prior Office decisions or restart the reexamination. If a party timely files an alert but lacks a right of entry under the rules (e.g., third party requester has no right to reply), the Office may waive rules to the extent necessary to enter and consider the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer Procedure for Reexamination Requests Between Art Units
rubrics_metrics.description: If the assigned CRU SPE believes the reexamination should be assigned to another art unit, consent of the CRU SPE of the desired art unit must be obtained; transfers must be made expeditiously consistent with 35 U.S.C. 305 special dispatch requirements, with hand-carrying of paper files as appropriate and CRU Director resolving unresolved conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 'new' art unit accepts assignment, the new CRU SPE assigns the request to an examiner in that unit. Emphasis on special dispatch and prompt resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Reporting for Reexamination Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel must report all time expended on reexamination activities on their Time and Attendance Reports because reexamination fees are based on full cost recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include time for supervision, copying, typing, docketing, and other activities related to reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-Initiated Reexamination Authority and Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may initiate ex parte reexamination at any time during the enforceability period of a patent if the Director determines a substantial new question of patentability is raised by patents or printed publications discovered or brought to attention, and may do so without a request or fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to order Director-initiated reexamination are rare and made only in compelling circumstances after review of all facts. Authority delegated to Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy; may also be made by Director, Deputy Director, or Commissioner for Patents. Determination becomes part of the official file and will be mailed to the patent owner per §1.33(c). Normally requests from outside the Office asking Director to undertake reexamination will not be considered.
